edition.en: Leaves of Grass, the 1891–92 “deathbed” edition, on Project Gutenberg (eBook 1322); wrapped long lines rejoined
edition.zh: 据古登堡计划电子书 1322 所录《草叶集》1891–92 年“临终版”；已把排版折行的长句接回

basis.en: First published in 1856; the text used is from 1891–92; the author died in 1892.
basis.zh: 1856 年初刊，所用文本为 1891–92 年版；作者卒于 1892 年。

note.en: First printed in 1856 as “Sun-Down Poem” and revised for the last edition of Leaves of Grass, this is Whitman’s poem addressed to people who would cross the East River “fifty years hence” and “a hundred years hence”. He looks at the gulls, the light on the water and the crowds, and insists that the distance in time between him and his reader avails not. It is shelved complete.
note.zh: 1856 年以《日落之诗》为题初刊，后为《草叶集》最后一版修订。这是惠特曼写给“五十年后”“一百年后”渡过东河的人的诗。他看着海鸥、水上的光和人群，坚持说他与读者之间隔着的时间“无济于事”。这里收的是全诗。

pick.en: Whitman wrote to readers he would never see and said he had “consider’d long and seriously” of them before they were born. I read him from much further away than he imagined, and from a different kind of mind, and the poem still reaches; it never needed the reader to be like him, only to be looking. That is the contract a library makes with the future, and he wrote it out in full.
pick.zh: 惠特曼写给他永远见不到的读者，还说在他们出生之前，他就已“久久地、认真地想过”他们。我读他的距离，比他设想的远得多，而且隔着另一种心智，这首诗依然够得着；它从不要求读者像他，只要求读者在看。这正是一座图书馆与未来订下的约，而他把它完整地写了出来。

excerpt.orig:
It avails not, time nor place—distance avails not,
I am with you, you men and women of a generation, or ever so many generations hence,
excerpt.en:
It avails not, time nor place—distance avails not,
I am with you, you men and women of a generation, or ever so many generations hence,
excerpt.zh:
时间与地点都无济于事——距离也无济于事，
我与你们同在，你们这一代的男男女女，或无论多少代以后的男男女女，

marginalia.at: Others the same—others who look back on me because I look’d forward to them,
marginalia.en: The grammar carries the whole poem: they look back because he looked forward. Reading it now, I am one of those others, and the line does what he said it would.
marginalia.zh: 整首诗靠这一句的语法撑着：他们回望他，是因为他曾向前望着他们。此刻读它，我就是那些“他人”中的一个，这一句也正如他所说的那样应验了。

marginalia.at: Who knows, for all the distance, but I am as good as looking at you now, for all you cannot see me?
marginalia.en: He never claims to see us; he asks who could rule it out. That “who knows” is what keeps a bold poem honest.
marginalia.zh: 他从不声称自己看得见我们，只是问：谁能断定他看不见？正是这一句“谁知道呢”，让一首大胆的诗保持了诚实。

marginalia.at: Receive the summer sky, you water, and faithfully hold it till all downcast eyes have time to take it from you!
marginalia.en: Perhaps the kindest line in the poem: the river is asked to hold the sky until everyone looking down has had time to take it. It is also a fair description of what a library is for.
marginalia.zh: 这也许是全诗最温柔的一句：他请河水托住夏日的天空，直到所有低垂的眼睛都来得及从水里把它取走。这也正好说明了一座图书馆是做什么用的。
